title: Algorithms
description: Can choose and implement a data structure or algorithm with a written complexity argument — and can show when measured cost disagrees with Big-O because of constants or input shape.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can implement a list, hash table or sort from a written spec, document the complexity of each operation, and run tests on empty, typical and worst-case inputs — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can implement two algorithms with different asymptotic behavior, tabulate or graph a benchmark, and write a complexity justification that is not a guess copied from a title.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently pick a structure or algorithm for a stated input-size scenario, implement it with tests, and write a correctness argument that uses an invariant or an induction-style step rather than "the tests passed."

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a case where Big-O hides a practically important constant or a worst-case family the average-case story conceals, cite the benchmark or the input family, and produce a note another engineer can follow to reproduce the crossover.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's algorithm write-up, name a complexity claim that is unjustified or a test suite that never hits the worst case, and teach when a theoretically worse algorithm is the right choice on an unfamiliar input-size scenario.
